role: first scripted-orchestrator workflow; the graph is fixed in code and only the leaf decisions use models
claim: Typed-decision models are sold as the decision layer of agent workflows, but they are benchmarked one isolated decision at a time. This workflow chains three decisions per customer turn over a five-turn session, with a gold answer at every node, and compares ways of assigning the nodes to models and of passing context between them. Written before any session was scored. The Banking77 test items inside the sessions have been scored before as isolated items by every system used here.

sessions.construction: Each turn is out of scope with probability 0.2. An in-scope turn that has an earlier in-scope turn in its session repeats that turn's intent with probability 0.3, using a different test utterance of the same intent; otherwise it draws an utterance of a different intent. No utterance is used twice.

scope.question: Is the current message a request that a retail bank's customer support can handle?
scope.gold: true for Banking77 turns, false for CLINC150 out-of-scope turns

repeat.question: Is the current message about the same issue as the most recent earlier banking request in this conversation?
repeat.asked: in-scope turns that have an earlier in-scope turn

success.turn: every node asked on that turn is right; a turn judged out of scope by the policy is not asked the later nodes, so a wrong scope decision fails the turn

context_forms.typed_state: no text is passed back; the repeat node compares the policy's own intent decision for this turn with its intent decision for the most recent earlier turn it judged in scope

policies.jev_raw_history: one Jev request per turn with all three questions and the raw history as state
policies.jev_typed_state: one Jev request per turn with the scope and intent questions and only the current message as state; repeat from typed state
policies.encoder_typed_state: Ettin encoder (float32 Banking77 checkpoint, seed 20261007) on the current message for intent; scope is its top probability against a threshold; repeat from typed state
policies.encoder_then_jev: encoder_typed_state, except that when the encoder's top probability is below the escalation threshold the turn's scope and intent come from the jev_typed_state answer for that turn
policies.gliclass_typed_state: the same construction as encoder_typed_state with GLiClass base
policies.decoder_typed_state: added 2026-10-10 before it was scored on any session: the same construction as encoder_typed_state with the float32 Banking77 Ettin decoder (seed 20261007) on the GPU
policies.decoder_then_jev: added 2026-10-10: decoder_typed_state with the same escalation rule as encoder_then_jev, using the decoder's own 25% dev quantile
policies.qwen4b_typed_state: added 2026-10-10 before it was scored on any session: the same construction with the suite's zero-shot Qwen3-4B readout and its Banking77 prior and temperature
policies.deepseek_typed_state: added 2026-10-11 before it was scored on any session: the typed-state construction with hosted DeepSeek v4.1 Flash, read by the api_protocol.json top-k tree readout with its Banking77 temperature
policies.qwen37_typed_state: added 2026-10-11 before it was scored on any session: the same with hosted Qwen3.7 Flash
policies.encoder_then_decoder: added 2026-10-11 before it was scored on any session: the encoder, escalating its low-confidence turns to the Ettin decoder's typed-state answer; no API call
policies.encoder_then_deepseek: added 2026-10-11 before it was scored on any session: the encoder, escalating its low-confidence turns to hosted DeepSeek v4.1 Flash's typed-state answer

thresholds.split: the 400 Program 1 Banking77 dev items as in-scope and the 100 CLINC150 out-of-scope validation queries as out-of-scope; no session item is used
thresholds.scope: the top-probability threshold with the best balanced accuracy on that split, for each local model
thresholds.escalation: the encoder top-probability value below which 25% of the in-scope dev items fall

jev_request.intent_instructions: Which label best describes the customer's current message?
jev_request.retry: 429, 503 and 529 and connection errors with backoff; a request still failing after 6 tries stops the run

metrics: accuracy at each node, on the turns where it is asked
turn success and session success with 95% bootstrap intervals over sessions
for typed-state repeat decisions: accuracy split by whether both intent decisions it depends on were right
Jev requests and input tokens per session; share of turns escalated
local latency is not timed here because local models run on the processor
not_in_v1: a model as orchestrator, Score nodes, and grounding nodes
hosted_note: Hosted workers see only the current message. Their scope threshold and escalation quantile come from the same dev split as the local workers. Their cost is recorded in artifacts/api/spend.json under the $20 project cap.
